abstract: The Albert algebra J = H3(O) is the 27-dimensional real Jordan algebra of 3x3 Hermitian octonionic matrices. An atom is an idempotent of trace one (a pure state). Its ideal yes-no test updates a state by the Lueders rule, and a word of outcomes has as probability the trace of the updated, unnormalised state. If finitely many atoms generate J, from any state no sequential projective representation on a real, complex or quaternionic Hilbert space reproduces all their word probabilities, and a finite linear inequality valid in every such representation fails by a positive margin from every state. Not generating J is equivalent to lying in a special unital subalgebra, and to one family of projections on C^6 or C^24 serving every state. For four generating atoms, from the maximally mixed state a representation on C^12 reproduces every word of length at most six, but none every word of length at most seven. A polynomial A in thirteen traces is nonnegative for four atoms and positive exactly when they generate J; its maximum is 4/19683, and when A = 0 every state has a representation on C^6. Three atoms never generate J, and every state has a representation on C^3. The atoms are exactly the primitive idempotents.

related_formalizations.note: PALOMAR-2026-10-16-000013 v1, same contributor. The fifteen modules under Glennie/ (compact octonions and Albert algebra as pairs of quaternions, product, trace, elementary laws, real conjugation, triality transport, automorphism compactness, diagonalisation and the square cone) are adapted from it; Glennie/Native.lean is the registered Glennie/Native.lean with two instances and one auxiliary declaration removed and one proof shortened, and the other fourteen descend from a later private version of the same code by the same contributor. None of that entry's compared conclusions is used as a hypothesis here, and no statement there is a compared statement here. Its Challenge defines the same compact octonions (same Cayley-Dickson convention) and Albert algebra as this Challenge, which defines them again because a Challenge may import only Mathlib.

Physlib (Apache-2.0), PhyslibAlpha/ProbabilisticTheory/JordanOrderUnit (Quadratic/Fundamental.lean, Power/Associative.lean, Operator.lean, Quadratic/Triple.lean); not a Palomar entry. Files by Tom Ole Diem. RealJordanFundamental.lean adapts 13 declarations of Quadratic/Fundamental.lean (the fundamental formula of the quadratic representation, by cyclic polarisation and derivation arguments; ambient class weakened to NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing, local operator definitions, namespaces and two endpoint names changed, proof bodies otherwise unchanged). JordanPowerAssociativity.lean adapts the 8 declarations of Power/Associative.lean (proof bodies identical after renaming). RealJordanOperators.lean adapts the definitions mulLeft, quadRep, innerDerivation, jordanTriple and six lemmas of Operator.lean and Quadratic/Triple.lean; for these two files the comparison was made against a local Physlib snapshot of October 2026, not the pinned commit. Each adapted file keeps the upstream copyright notice; the root LICENSE is the Apache-2.0 text, Physlib's licence; details are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and docs/ATTRIBUTION.md. UnitalJordanProduct, JordanProductQuadratic and EuclideanJordanForm follow its conventions without copying a declaration.

PALOMAR-2026-09-13-000001 v1, same contributor; split Albert algebra over a field of characteristic zero. No file is used here; it is an ancestor of code in PALOMAR-2026-10-16-000013 (general cubic-trace lemma), from which this repository adapts other files. No statement there is a statement here.
PALOMAR-2026-10-29-000034 v1, same contributor; local geometry of the tight 39-point code in OP2. Shares the Glennie ancestry; no file of it is used here and no statement there is a statement here.

B. Ehrlich, ehrlich-b/sequential-products-lean, Apache-2.0; related work by another author, no code used. PALOMAR-2026-08-22-000006 v1 (TwistNormalForm.real_classification, TwistNormalForm.complex_classification: sequential products in van de Wetering's sense on H_N(R) are the Lueders product, on H_N(C) with N >= 3 they have the twist normal form) and PALOMAR-2026-08-21-000009 v1 (AlbertPowerAssoc.jpow_mul_jpow: Albert's power-associativity theorem for commutative Jordan rings carrying a real-module structure), both at this commit; at 3c0e870eb2acb1320b62e62c791c9365f7e5260b the same repository is registered as PALOMAR-2026-08-21-000001 v1 (WignerReal.exists_isometry_of_transProbPreserving, the real case of Wigner's theorem). The classifications describe the update on a given algebra; the statements here concern which statistics of given ideal tests under the Lueders update a Hilbert space reproduces. This repository proves power associativity of its general Jordan products (JordanPowerAssociativity, adapted from Physlib), not from this entry. Cited in the core paper.

B. Ehrlich, ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan, Apache-2.0; related work by another author, no code used. At this commit PALOMAR-2026-08-23-000005 v1 (KoecherAlfsenShultz.orderIso_preservesJordan: a unital linear order isomorphism of a Euclidean Jordan algebra is a Jordan automorphism) and PALOMAR-2026-08-23-000006 v1 (JordanSpectral.spectral_resolution_bilinear); at a0077822f037d5de7bdcbf3f9f498cc00f361a4a PALOMAR-2026-08-29-000001 v1 (JordanTraceForm.traceForm_comm, traceForm_assoc, traceForm_self_nonneg, traceForm_self_eq_zero_iff); at a83407e4dbf73c77c31a2291c02f20b37a5ebbaf PALOMAR-2026-08-29-000008 v1 (JordanFramePeirce.frameBlock_isInternal, finrank_frameBlock_diag: the Peirce decomposition relative to a Jordan frame). This repository proves its own spectral resolution and Peirce decomposition (JordanSpectralResolution, JordanPeirceFusion) in a different setting. Cited in the core paper.

B. Ehrlich, ehrlich-b/composition-algebras, Apache-2.0; PALOMAR-2026-08-29-000018 v1 (Hurwitz's classification: a nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra over R is isomorphic to R, C, the quaternions or the octonions, with all four constructed). Ten files are adapted whole into src/CompositionAlgebras (Composition/Defs, Composition/Doubling, Composition/CayleyDickson, Composition/Instances, Composition/Isomorphisms, Composition/Hurwitz, Composition/Classification, Octonions, OctonionTrace, OctonionModule): ported to the Lean module system, one deprecated Mathlib import replaced, redundant tactic combinators and simp arguments removed in Composition/Isomorphisms; each keeps the upstream copyright header, and the upstream licence text is src/CompositionAlgebras/LICENSE. CompositionAlgebra.hurwitz_classification is used for the classification of the simple summands of rank three in core Theorem 4.11 (HurwitzRankThreeClassification). At e37e22b0571a170ba18a0d8db29fe2a857906b92 the same repository is registered as PALOMAR-2026-08-29-000015 v1 (Hurwitz's theorem in dimension form). The octonions of the Albert algebra here are this repository's own (Glennie/, adapted from PALOMAR-2026-10-16-000013, and the Challenge's Cayley-Dickson definition). Details in docs/ATTRIBUTION.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Cited in the core paper.

S. Alexander, stalex444/herstein-jordan-homomorphisms, MIT; related work by another author, no code used. PALOMAR-2026-11-11-000008 v1 (JordanPrime.jordan_onto_prime and five further theorems: Herstein's theorem, in Smiley's forms, that a Jordan homomorphism of associative rings onto a prime ring is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism, with the Jacobson-Rickart domain theorem and examples for each hypothesis). Both concern Jordan homomorphisms; the statement here (albertJordanHom_eq_zero) is that every Jordan homomorphism from the Albert algebra J into an associative algebra is zero, whose source is not an associative ring, and it uses no result of that entry.

M. J. Soares, The Albert algebra in Lean 4: Jordan identity and non-speciality, version 1.0.0, Zenodo, 22 July 2026, repository markkasaurus/albert-algebra-lean, Apache-2.0; not a Palomar entry; no code used. It proves the Jordan identity for H3(O), its real dimension 27, Glennie's identity in symmetrisations of associative algebras and an explicit violation in H3(O). This repository proves the Jordan identity of its own encoding of H3(O) (NativeAnalysis.jordan_identity) and that every Jordan homomorphism from J into an associative algebra is zero (albertJordanHom_eq_zero) independently, by another route. Cited in the core paper.
